review: law X4 r8 round 3 / J1 successor S11

priorFindings.reason: FC records every existing source's first cause with the latch, CertainRefusal preserves operation-stopped, and LD8-9 gates J3b cancellation code/J-C15/J-C15b on X4-F3 acceptance and integration before or with J3b. Both D8-1 schedules retain their cause, row and REV reason.
W-5 still names step 3, admit refusal, observer tick and both boundary failure/AlreadyStopped paths, with seams outside the cause critical section.

S11.6:405-429 and LD8-10 require start to create the empty record, rebind all monitor stop authority, read the gate under the cause lock, then refuse a latched gate before guard creation or observer spawn. The exact successful-first-read/unrelated-unwind schedule reaches the existing Live(FailStop { latched }) row. W-9 pins the entry order and removal of bare latches; W-11 and W-12 cover the unwind schedule, all three lease-free handles, and the clear-entry control.

S11.6:463-469, LD8-2:640-644, LD8-6:692 and W-10:563-568 explicitly allow cause-lock acquisition to contend, assert only no monitor-lock wait by stop transitions, no I/O/wait while cause is held, and no added cause-lock wait on successful admission. No timing bound or native scheduling qualification is claimed.

noAcceptedOutcomeChangedBasis: The accepted r7 text is preserved apart from the declared title/acceptance note. Round 3 establishes I1 at the actual entry using the existing Live(FailStop { latched }) row; it changes no accepted row, reason or outcome as an exception. FC, CertainRefusal, existing reason/row mappings, X2 handoff ordering and the declared S11 gate changes retain their reviewed meanings.

entryProof.beforeCheck: consume LeaseFree and rebind every surviving monitor stop path to that record; no bare latch remains callable outside stop transitions
entryProof.latchedBranch: read under cause lock; release and refuse on existing Live(FailStop(latched)), without guard, observer or record
entryProof.clearBranch: release and expose the rebound guard/observer; every possible subsequent latch records only when first under cause
entryProof.linearization: The clear checked state establishes the initial invariant. A stop by the newly spawned observer before the caller receives the guard is a lawful protected post-entry stop.
implementationObligations: No raw stop-handle escape or clone surviving outside the transition
Rebind before checked load; observer spawn after cause-lock release
No clock/counter callback or monitor read while cause is held
Map entry-latched refusal to Live while retaining Observer(io::Error) for thread-spawn failure
Keep monotonic word and monitor history; no clear, reset, cause seeding or new row

questions.reason: The prior counterexample remains possible before start: StopOnUnwind may latch a successful first read during unrelated unwinding. The entry rule now catches that bit and refuses with Live(FailStop { subject: latched }), without a guard, observer or record. Rebinding precedes the checked load. LeaseFree owns the gate/observer/monitor handles; the admitted-read callback receives only the sample and cannot retain stop authority. The handoff carries that owned LeaseFree into start, with no other monitor call between the read and start. Once consumed/rebound, no production bare handle can latch between check and installation. W-9 makes this a required implementation pin.

The gate is never cleared or rearmed, successful-read history is carried unchanged, and StopOnUnwind remains conservative before and after entry. The new refusal uses the existing OperationRefusal.Live -> StopCause.FailStop -> ObserverFailStop mapping and latched subject. It is not CertainRefusal or an invariant exception. The handoff has not produced ProjectOperation or CommitSession, so no StoppedSession/reserve exists and no end-path REV is owed. Existing handoff cleanup releases built owners in reverse order; existing thread-spawn errors retain their separate Observer mapping.

Source 4 is now defined by the actual Drop predicate: a read/boundary check ends while its thread is panicking. It includes callback-origin unwinding and successful methods invoked during unrelated unwinding. The lease-free case is bare and refused at entry; the post-entry case uses the stop handle and records FailStop(latched) only if it is first. A repeat unwind latch after a normal failure likewise cannot replace the earlier source's cause.

X4-F3 owns OperationGuard.start and its monitor stop binding. Adding the entry check there and one handoff mapping arm is consistent with that ownership. The existing Live row already maps first-read AlreadyStopped, and the handoff order, transferred owners, fence/lease cleanup and other refusals do not change. S11.12's X2 record is sufficient; no new X2 law decision is introduced.

The three properties are explicit and matched by W-10. Cause acquisition may contend; it does not acquire the monitor mutex or hold cause over monitor I/O. Successful admission does not take cause. The entry check uses a short cause section before the observer is spawned. Native scheduling and syscall timing remain excluded. These are protocol/ownership constraints, not elapsed-time guarantees.

W-11 exercises the exact successful lease-free read during unrelated unwinding and checks Live(FailStop(latched)), no guard/observer, no record, state 2 and retained successful-read history; it also checks the rebound post-entry counterpart. W-12 injects a bare latch through each of the three handles immediately before start and includes a clear-state control whose first transition records its cause. W-9 pins record -> rebind -> checked load -> spawn and excludes surviving bare latch access. The stated synchronization seams are outside critical sections. No control was executed during this law review.

FC and the stop-transition steps, CertainRefusal's row/reason mapping, source-pair controls, X4-F3/J3b split, X3d record item and LD8-9 gate remain. Once entry succeeds, I1 is inductive because only the first setter inserts while holding cause and every reader serializes with that insertion. If the observer records a first stop before start returns, it does so through the rebound transition and I1 still holds. The entry proof does not promise perpetual state 0. No cause -> monitor lock edge is added, and the earlier word/CAS bounds remain.

Every r7 line survives verbatim except title r7 -> r8 and the exact 35-byte history acceptance note. The reviewed round-2 word/state sections, FC/transition, cause mappings, CertainRefusal and landing gate are byte-identical. Round 3 removes the prior reachable invariant-row fallback for the bare unwind latch and selects the existing fail-stop row before any guard/session. No accepted row, reason, outcome, permit, gate law, X2 handoff order, host projection or reserve is changed apart from declared S11 changes.

LD8-10 decides only the missing entry obligation in X4's guard. It rejects reset, CertainRefusal, invariant exception, loss of conservative unwind stopping and an incomplete first-read-only check. No new public vocabulary, crash point, durability point, budget or independent law is introduced. Acceptance is for the law's pinned bytes; X4-F3 and J3b still require their specified implementation reviews, source pins, controls and serialized lead sets.

validation.method: Read-only source inspection and digest/diff audit; no product code or behavioral model executed
